```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Facility_Location")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 300)

    # Problem Data
    facilities = list(range(13))  # F0..F12
    customers = list(range(31))  # C0..C30

    # Facility coordinates (x, y)
    facility_coords = [(74, 12), (31, 93), (77, 9), (38, 95), (35, 47), (84, 91), (52, 91), (83, 24), (88, 2), (53, 24), (15, 50), (43, 57), (69, 33)]

    # Customer coordinates (x, y)
    customer_coords = [(37, 50), (85, 20), (39, 9), (71, 35), (2, 24), (98, 64), (50, 53), (79, 67), (36, 93), (87, 5), (15, 74), (42, 5), (77, 64), (99, 75), (56, 86), (70, 18), (21, 84), (5, 61), (74, 17), (42, 41), (11, 65), (68, 34), (12, 80), (70, 9), (7, 24), (80, 15), (60, 65), (87, 76), (25, 25), (97, 54), (77, 2)]

    facility_capacities = [190.0, 151.0, 77.0, 186.0, 105.0, 181.0, 127.0, 145.0, 82.0, 148.0, 193.0, 176.0, 142.0]
    customer_demands = [22.0, 31.0, 47.0, 13.0, 34.0, 28.0, 29.0, 50.0, 12.0, 17.0, 12.0, 32.0, 49.0, 14.0, 48.0, 28.0, 27.0, 35.0, 21.0, 12.0, 47.0, 42.0, 48.0, 15.0, 34.0, 17.0, 33.0, 35.0, 43.0, 26.0, 38.0]
    fixed_costs = [376.0, 161.0, 112.0, 322.0, 485.0, 482.0, 452.0, 110.0, 413.0, 485.0, 201.0, 477.0, 472.0]
    transport_rate = 0.5  # $/km/unit

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates (INDUCED COSTS)
    def euclidean_distance(coord1, coord2):
        return math.sqrt((coord1[0] - coord2[0])**2 + (coord1[1] - coord2[1])**2)

    distances = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            distances[(i, j)] = euclidean_distance(facility_coords[i], customer_coords[j])

    # Decision Variables
    # Open_F{i}: Binary - whether facility i is opened
    open_facility = {}
    for i in facilities:
        open_facility[i] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Open_F{i}")

    # Ship_F{i}_C{j}: Continuous - units shipped from facility i to customer j
    ship = {}
    for i in facilities:
        for j in customers:
            ship[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_F{i}_C{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize fixed costs + transport costs
    # Transport cost = distance * rate * units shipped
    obj = quicksum(fixed_costs[i] * open_facility[i] for i in facilities)
    obj += quicksum(
        distances[(i, j)] * transport_rate * ship[(i, j)]
        for i in facilities for j in customers
    )
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # Demand satisfaction constraints
    for j in customers:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for i in facilities) >= customer_demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_C{j}"
        )

    # Capacity constraints (can only ship if facility is open)
    for i in facilities:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(ship[(i, j)] for j in customers) <= facility_capacities[i] * open_facility[i],
            name=f"Capacity_F{i}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Team,

We need to decide which warehouses to open and how to route product to customers across our network. We are evaluating 13 candidate warehouse sites and planning service to 31 customer locations. The candidate warehouse map points are listed in Facility Coordinates:

  - C26: (60, 65)
  - C27: (87, 76)
  - C28: (25, 25)
  - C29: (97, 54)
  - C30: (77, 2). Distances between facilities and customers are calculated as straight-line (Euclidean) distances from the map coordinates.

Opening any warehouse commits us to a one-time cost reflected in [376.0, 161.0, 112.0, 322.0, 485.0, 482.0, 452.0, 110.0, 413.0, 485.0, 201.0, 477.0, 472.0]. Moving product from an open warehouse to a customer is charged at our transport rate, 0.5, with spend scaling according to both how far we ship and how many units we move.

Each warehouse has a ceiling on how much volume it can handle; these limits are provided in [190.0, 151.0, 77.0, 186.0, 105.0, 181.0, 127.0, 145.0, 82.0, 148.0, 193.0, 176.0, 142.0]. Each customer has a required volume that must be fully satisfied; those needs are captured in [22.0, 31.0, 47.0, 13.0, 34.0, 28.0, 29.0, 50.0, 12.0, 17.0, 12.0, 32.0, 49.0, 14.0, 48.0, 28.0, 27.0, 35.0, 21.0, 12.0, 47.0, 42.0, 48.0, 15.0, 34.0, 17.0, 33.0, 35.0, 43.0, 26.0, 38.0].

A few operating rules guide the decision:
- A warehouse can only ship if we choose to open it.
- Every customer’s demand must be met in full.
- Shipments out of any warehouse cannot exceed that site’s capacity.

The objective is to minimize our total cost—facility opening costs plus distance-driven shipping costs—while meeting every customer’s demand within the available capacity. Practically, this means balancing trade-offs: opening fewer warehouses can save on fixed costs but may force longer hauls to reach certain customers, while opening more sites reduces travel distance at the expense of higher fixed outlays. Capacity limits may require spreading volume across multiple sites, and some customers may be best served by the closest open warehouse, whereas others might create cost pressure unless a nearer site is activated.

Our deliverable will be a recommended set of warehouses to open, customer-to-warehouse shipping assignments, expected utilization at each open site, and a clear view of the resulting total cost under the assumptions above.
